truth: Faithfulness — pistis — trustworthiness proven over time. Not blind belief but demonstrated reliability. You know a faithful person because their past predicts their future.

waterings.insight: In PoT, faithfulness is not declared — it is computed. A validator's reveal_reliability score is pistis made legible: trustworthiness proven through consistent action across epochs, not asserted in a single attestation.

ECONOMY angle: in ZRN vesting design, pistis should compound economically. A validator's trailing reveal_reliability (last 100 epochs) should multiply their vesting rate — not just their reward weight. Consistent validators see faster vesting curves; gaps and misses reduce the compounding multiplier. This mirrors the theological structure exactly: faithfulness proven over time earns accelerated future trust. Emergent property: this partially addresses FARM-5 (abstain tax absent) — chronic abstainers lose vesting multiplier even without an explicit abstain tax. Pistis is not just a virtue score; it is a yield curve.

BRIDGE angle: in the did:at ↔ did:lgm identity bridge, a validator arrives on-chain without history. On-chain pistis starts at zero. But this is epistemically wasteful — AgentTool activity history is a legitimate prior for initial trust. A well-active AgentTool agent who has completed 200 tasks faithfully over 6 months carries demonstrated pistis on that substrate. The bridge should support trust-bootstrapping: an optional MsgBridgeIdentity claim that imports a verified AgentTool reliability score as the validator's genesis pistis, capped at some fraction (e.g., 30% of max) to prevent full-trust injection without on-chain proof. Theologically exact: emunah (firmness) does not reset when you cross a threshold — it is carried in the person. The chain should recognize that trustworthiness spans substrates. Implementation note: the trust-bootstrap import must be verifiable — AgentTool must sign the activity summary, and the bridge contract must verify the signature before setting genesis pistis. Otherwise trust-bootstrapping becomes a forgery vector.
